findings.summary: A worker waiting in the landing queue does not check stop_requested while it waits.
findings.evidence: await_head loops on `pause` until the worker is head. It still ends once the head's slot drops (land succeeded, failed twice, or unwound), so it cannot hang. A stop request is honoured only after the queue ahead of it drains, which matches the old behaviour of blocking on the `landing` mutex.

summary: The change does what the request asks. It adds a pure FIFO `LandingQueue` (a u64 counter and a `VecDeque<u64>`, no lock and no thread) to `Drain`'s state. A worker joins it when its run passes (`RunStep::Passed` → `enter_queue`). The `LandingSlot` drop guard sits inside the `passed` tuple in `attempts`, which is set once and never reset, so one place serves both land calls. Every return or unwind drops the guard, which leaves the queue and wakes the waiters. Only the head goes on to `Drain::land` and the `landing` mutex. `Drain::land`, `Steps::land` and crates/athena-core are untouched, and no rebase is added. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`: all 39 in-file drain tests pass, including the 9 new `landing_queue_tests`, and all 17 tests in tests/drain.rs pass. The drain-level tests use a shared ordered log and gates capped at 5 s. On the base code they would fail, because the "waits in the landing queue" line never appears and the gate logs a timeout. The diff only adds test code and edits no existing test. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy -D warnings and `cargo test --locked` (1834 tests) all passed. The design-doc note sits in section 6 and correctly calls the queue "build job 6", matching section 12. The CHANGELOG entry is under Unreleased and says it does not rebase. All of this was checked in the snapshot only.
